paraphrase: Śamatha and vipaśyanā are the basis of all meditation in sūtra and tantra; the general presentation explains their causes, kinds and results before the special Mahāmudrā.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.

paraphrase: The preliminaries of Mahāmudrā: the common ones (the four thoughts), the uncommon ones (refuge and bodhicitta, Vajrasattva, maṇḍala offering, guru yoga), and above all devotion to the guru, through whose blessing realization arises.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.

paraphrase: Śamatha in Mahāmudrā: first with a support (a small object, the breath, a deity's body), then without support, balancing tightness and looseness; the faults of dullness and agitation are recognized and corrected.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.

paraphrase: The nine ways of settling the mind (the nine stages of calm abiding) are presented as they apply to Mahāmudrā śamatha.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Recalled in outline only.

paraphrase: Vipaśyanā: the meditator examines the mind at rest and in movement — its colour, shape and location, where it arises, stays and goes, whether the still and the moving mind are the same or different — and, not finding it, recognizes its empty and luminous nature.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.

paraphrase: The four ways of deviating from emptiness — deviating from its essence, deviating into sealing (stamping things as empty), deviating into the antidote, and deviating into the path — and the three strayings, attachment to bliss, clarity and non-thought, which lead to rebirth in the desire, form and formless realms.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.

paraphrase: The four yogas — one-pointedness, simplicity (freedom from elaboration), one taste and non-meditation — each divided into lesser, middling and greater, twelve in all; at each, meditative experience (nyams) is distinguished from realization (rtogs pa).
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.

paraphrase: How the four yogas correspond to the five paths and ten grounds is set out with the differing views of earlier Kagyu masters (e.g. whether the path of seeing is reached with simplicity or later).
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Low: the specific correlations of each master are not recalled reliably.

paraphrase: The fruition is the dharmakāya realized in non-meditation: nothing new is produced; the mind's nature, which was always so, is fully manifest.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally.

paraphrase: Two ways of meditating are taught according to the person: the scholar's analytical meditation and the simple meditator's resting meditation; both are used, alternating as the student needs.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Terms dpyad sgom / 'jog sgom (paṇḍita's / kusulu's meditation); recalled in substance.
